spans.text: Flight.
Her mind is consumed by this single thought.
She dashes through the busy, filthy streets, her feet stepping into puddles and splashing water everywhere. Meanwhile, the murderous shrieks remain hot on her heels.
Liar! Kill her!
Don't let that shameless whore go!
The hysterical howls sound terrifyingly close.
Her breath is erratic and her legs feel heavy as lead, but the street seems to stretch on and on.
Ma'am, this way!
A hand stretches out from a dark alley and grasps her own tightly.
It looks almost exactly like a human hand, but she can immediately tell that it belongs to a Doll.
Who are you? Where are you taking me?
Follow me!
She follows the Doll's instruction and resumes her strenuous run.
The view brightens until it becomes dazzling to the eye...
...Halloween, in a remote and isolated private sanatorium.
Miss Fuduto, are you awake?
Hm... Did I fall asleep in the middle of reading...?
...The silence outside the window is broken by a roar of thunder, followed by the splattering of heavy rain.
The Doll carer immediately drops what she is doing and walks over to close the window.
It's really coming down!
Heavy rain, just like in her dream.
Fuduto is reminded of her troubling nightmare.
She recalls the frenzied howls and her murderous pursuer, and her heart sinks.
Just then, there is a knock on the door.
Hello, who are you, if I may ask?
Sorry for the intrusion. I am TAC-50, a Griffin T-Doll. I just completed a mission and am on my way back to base.
My navigation system malfunctioned in the thunderstorm and led me here by mistake, and my power level is running dangerously low...
I'm wondering if you would allow me to recharge here; I am very happy to pay, of course!
What do you think, Miss Fuduto?
In her dream, a hand stretched out of the dark alley and clasped her hand.
A Doll's hand.
Hm? A Doll...?
It's pouring out there, so let her in.
Everyone deserves a happy Halloween, human or Doll.
Please come in.
Thank you, Miss Fuduto.
You're very welcome. The charging port is over there.
There are some Halloween candy on the table, please help yourself if you like.
Sure, thanks again.
Fuduto watches as TAC-50 walks toward the charging port and quietly instructs her Doll carer.
Keep an eye on her. When she's charged up, see her off right away.
Understood.
Fuduto turns and returns to the other room. She picks up the book that she has just put down.
Um, hello. Is this the port?
Yes, you may use it.
Right, thanks.
TAC-50 finds the charging port and plugs herself in.
"In this mansion at the edge of the world..."
"Phantoms sigh when the night is deep."
"Stay vigilant, beware of strangers."
"They speak of legends about a reflection."
Fuduto's hand freezes in the middle of flipping a page at the sound notification.
Hm? What is with that charging notification?
The latest update released by IOP allows charging notification customizations. Everyone back at base is messing around with theirs.
Why don't you download the update? You might be able to change yours too.
Let me try!
The Doll carer plugs herself into the update port with excitement.
Hm, it's a shame, but I don't seem to be eligible for this update...
Anyway, what's the song that you're using? It sounds really familiar...
It's a song from the musical "Butterfly in a Cocoon" that I love very much.
Oh, no wonder! Isn't that the song Miss Fuduto is always play—
Ahem.
Uh, never mind.
Well, the rain isn't letting up, is it...?
Noticing the Doll carer's discomfort, TAC-50 changes the subject politely.
It was such a cool and dry night, then it just started pouring. The weather has been rather strange lately.
You're right. Who would've thought it would start raining so heavily on my way back...
Speaking of which, where is your base? I may know a better route for you to get home.
Hm... I will be making a detour first...
To tell you the truth, I was planning to attend a memorial service for my favorite musical actress.
TAC-50 lifts her dripping cape and reveals a carefully protected bouquet.
It's a bunch of red roses in full bloom. The bloody crimson burns vibrantly in the Doll's eyes.
Red roses? They look wonderful...
Wait, do humans use red roses for memorial services?
Not in the usual case, but this musical actress had a very strong predilection for red roses.
Fuduto, who is sitting in the study, flinches at TAC-50's remark, but she does not turn her head.
Could this actress happen to be...
Miss Passadou, best known for her performance in "Butterfly in a Cocoon".
I knew it. I've heard a lot about Miss Passadou.
It's such a pity that I never had the chance to watch her perform live. Everyone said she was an exceptional actress.
Both the musical she starred in and her life story were tragically beautiful...
Indeed. The stage has seen countless musical actors, but only a handful have made their mark in history.
It has been a year after Miss Passadou's death, but many people are still talking about her.
Really?
(Sighs) We are hardly up-to-date with these things living in such a remote place. What do people out there talk about her?
Fuduto silently slips over to the doorway of her study, listening intently to TAC-50's reply.
Hm... How should I put it?
Is it so difficult to explain?
Not exactly... It's just...
I don't really know where to begin...
The Doll carer nods in bemusement. But then she remembers TAC-50's considerate gesture and decides to return the favor by ending this awkward conversation.
Let's talk about something else. We don't have guests very often, why don't you fill me in on the latest news?
Sure.
Fuduto frowns and finally resolves to come out of the study.
...Is there anything you need, ma'am?
For goodness' sake, you see that rain outside? Even a Tactical Doll has to find shelter, God knows how the flowers in the garden will fare.
Apologies! I'll get them inside right now!
The Doll carer rushes out into the downpour.
What were you two chattering about? I hope I didn't interrupt anything.
Not at all, Miss Fuduto.
We were just talking about Miss Passadou, a musical actress whom I admire very much...
Oh?
Are you also a fan?
Um, this might be a bit impertinent...
But you look very much like Miss Passadou. Are you perhaps a family relation?
Hahaha, no way! She was a star!
You're not the first to note our physical resemblance, but sadly I have neither her grace nor her God-gifted voice.
The moment I saw you, I genuinely hoped that you...
You must really admire this Passadou...
Come, keep me company on this dull, rainy night. It has been a while since we last had guests.
I'd love to! I'm always happy to share what I know about Miss Passadou!
...In Fuduto's room.
The bedroom is furnished as a simple medical ward. TAC-50 can even detect the scent of disinfectant in the air.
Are you ill, Miss Fuduto?
It's nothing serious. The doctor prescribed peace and quiet, that's why I'm here in the middle of nowhere.
I see...
TAC-50 helps Fuduto lie down and carefully props her against her pillows.
Thank you.
Don't mention it. I'm glad to help.
So what were you talking about?
We discussed Miss Passadou's favorite flower, her best-known work...
Hm, and that people are still talking about her after her death.
...Do you also enjoy musicals, Miss Fuduto?
You can say that.
I don't remember when I got into the genre, but I have watched "Butterfly in a Cocoon".
Your charging notification is an excerpt from one of the songs, isn't it?
That's right, I adore "Butterfly in a Cocoon".
Miss Passadou was absolutely amazing in the role of the wife.
Not only was her singing beautiful, she conveyed all the emotions perfectly in her performance.
I remember it was incredibly difficult to get tickets to her shows back then.
Every single performance was sold out almost immediately.
It was her best work, after all.
People have always been mesmerized by Miss Passadou.
I believe she will endure in the people's memory even in the future.
What makes you so sure? There hasn't been any news about her for a quite a while now, after all...
Are you aware of the fire at the theater on Halloween last year, during Miss Passadou's farewell show?
I've heard about it.
Due to her poor health, Miss Passadou started performing less and less frequently.
Meanwhile, a supporting actress called Jane Doe stood in for her and stole the heart of Mr. Arla – the theater's proprietor and Miss Passadou's husband.
Yes, that was the talk of the town back then.
To completely replace Passadou, this Jane Doe even surgically altered her appearance in Passadou's likeness and plotted her murder.
When poor Miss Passadou found out, she decided to give one last performance, then she would die in the theater at her most beautiful moment.
Unfortunately, Mr. Arla also died in the fire while trying to save his wife. And Jane Doe was never seen again.
Despicable woman.
However, that was what people believed previously.
You mean people now believe differently?
Yeah...
A new version of these events have been circulating recently.
But this new account is complete slander against Miss Passadou and it makes me so angry to hear it...
TAC-50 stares bitterly out the window. The rain leaves delicate streaks of tears on the glass.
...What are they saying?
Fuduto tries desperately to suppress her emotions, her icy fingertips digging deep into her palms.
